page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Optimized3.Flex.8-64 is a flexible compute instance belonging to the Optimized instance family. The server is built on the x86_64 architecture and is powered by an Intel Xeon 6354 processor operating at a base frequency of 3.0 GHz. The system provides 8 physical cores and 16 vCPUs through symmetric multithreading, utilizing dedicated CPU thread allocation rather than shared or burstable capacity.

Memory capacity is configured at 64.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, meaning all persistent storage requirements must be met using external block storage attachments. Additionally, the instance contains no dedicated GPU hardware accelerators. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

From an infrastructure perspective, the 1:4 processor-to-memory ratio provides a standard operational balance for workloads requiring predictable core performance without overpaying for unused memory or local flash storage. Because the instance relies on network-attached storage and contains no discrete graphics hardware, it delivers cost-efficient resource density tailored toward sustained CPU processing. Recommended workloads include backend web services, continuous integration and build nodes, containerized application clusters, and enterprise microservices.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Optimized3.Flex.8-64 is a compute instance in the Optimized family powered by an Intel Xeon 6354 processor operating at 3.0 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture, it delivers 8 physical cores and 16 dedicated vCPUs paired with 64.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The configuration features zero local disk storage, requiring external block storage for persistent data, and does not include GPU acceleration. It includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. With dedicated thread allocation and consistent clock frequencies, this configuration avoids the latency variability found in shared-core instances. It presents an efficient allocation profile for enterprise computing requirements that do not necessitate attached NVMe storage, making it suitable for web application hosting, intermediate ETL pipelines, build automation, and general containerized services.
